summary: People-pleasing drains you and erodes your credibility: each time you bend your answer to match the asker, your 'yes' loses all value. By contrast, people with a fixed stance are the ones remembered. The call to action: stop reshaping yourself for an audience that won't applaud anyway — pick one direction and hold it.
themes: choosing and committing to one direction
importantPhrases: change your answer to match whoever asked
an audience that will not applaud anyway
choose one direction and stay with it
visualOpportunities: A figure physically bending/stretching like a shape-shifter between different faces — literal 'changing your answer'
An hourglass or draining battery draining faster with each added person — accumulating tiredness
A rubber stamp whose imprint gets fainter with each press — 'yes' losing meaning
A mirror that keeps re-morphing to reflect different people instead of one face — self-erasure
A lighthouse or straight arrow holding steady while everything else sways — the steadfast ones who get remembered
A theater of empty seats / un-clapping hands — the audience that won't applaud anyway
A forked path collapsing into a single straight line — choose one direction
A torn-up draft of yourself, editing marks crossed out — 'stop editing yourself'
A compass locking onto one bearing — committing to a direction
A metronome or plumb line standing rigid amid chaos — consistency as strength
